title: Lean core: one std outbound HTTP client for the pillars; ureq leaves core
goal: Replace the ureq-based outbound client in crates/susi-http-transport (http_call, http_call_with_body, http_post_utf8; used by GEMI BYOK providers, gemi-models downloads, GMCP, GAWD peers and the harness gateway) with HTTP/1.1 on std sockets and exactly one verified TLS stack, keeping certificate and hostname verification, the total deadline, redirect policy, proxy behaviour, SSE/chunked streaming and the error texts callers match on; delete susi-vendor-ureq; lower the pillar ceilings to the measured reach.
acceptance: cargo test --offline --locked --no-fail-fast -p susi-http-transport -p susi-adapters-llm -p susi-gemi-models -p susi-gawd-agents -p susi-gawd-a2a -p susi-gemi -p susi-harness -p susi-gmcp -p susi-server --lib
cargo test --offline --locked -p susi --test architecture_tests --test orphan_sources --test lean_core_ceilings --test core_docs_promise_no_ui_or_plugins --test no_github_coupling --test task_records
cold cargo build -j 8 --offline --locked -p susi, alternated with base bf0bb15a6
host: CEO laptop, CachyOS Linux x86_64, 28 threads, Rust 1.99.0 (pinned); other agents compiling (load average 10-18)
limitations: TLS is the platform stack (native-tls: Schannel / platform OpenSSL / Security.framework), not pure Rust: rustls needs rustls-webpki and untrusted (ISC) and webpki-roots (CDLA-Permissive-2.0), which deny.toml's strict licence list forbids, its offline providers are ring (C/asm) or aws-lc-rs (C), and openssl stays in the pillar closure anyway because GMCP, GEMI REST and A2A serve TLS through native-tls. A pure-Rust TLS needs a CEO licence decision and the server side moved together.

tokio, hyper, hyper-util, h2, mio, tokio-native-tls stay in the pillar closure: susi-gmcp, susi-gemi, susi-gawd and susi-harness depend on them directly (GMCP and harness servers, gemi async code), and susi-http-transport still hosts the server-side dual_transport/http_conn.
Connections are not pooled (ureq kept keep-alive connections per profile): every call opens a fresh TCP (+TLS) connection.
No Accept-Encoding: gzip is advertised and no gzip decoding exists; no caller relied on it.
A redirect hop is direct or proxied by its own host (loopback direct); ureq chose once from the first URL.
SOCKS proxies from the environment are not used (unchanged: ureq was built without its SOCKS feature).
Windows: compiled only through the workspace check on Linux; the TLS and socket tests have not been run on a Windows host.
